title: Rail freight transport dropped by 1.8% in 2025
key_claim: EU rail freight performance fell 1.8% in 2025 to 368.2 billion tonne-kilometres, the fourth consecutive annual decline, with decreases in 16 member states; Germany accounted for a third of the EU total.
frame_summary: Reports the 2025 fall as a continuation: a fourth consecutive annual decline in EU rail freight performance, spread across most member states, presented as data without advocacy.
verbatim_quote: in 2024 to 368.2 tkm, and marking the fourth consecutive year of decline
verbatim_list: In 2025, the EU rail freight transport performance fell by 1.8%, declining from 375.1 billion tonne-kilometres (tkm) in 2024 to 368.2 tkm, and marking the fourth consecutive year of decline.
Compared with 2024, rail freight transport performance measured in tonne-kilometres decreased in 16 EU countries, while 8 countries recorded an increase.
The largest decreases were recorded in Ireland (-35.2%), Latvia (-18.8%) and Estonia (-17.3%).
Germany remained by far the largest contributor to rail freight transport performance in the EU, with one third of the EU total (33.5%; 123.5 billion tkm).
notes: Official Eurostat news article on the rail_go dataset; the anchor for the EU-level decline framing.

title: Schienengüterverkehr trotz positiver Wirtschaftsentwicklung unter Druck
key_claim: Swiss transalpine rail freight grew 3.1% in H1 2026 but lost share to road, slipping to 68% of the market; alpine lorry crossings rose around 7% and single wagonload traffic carried 8% fewer loaded wagons, with SBB Cargo making a loss on it.
frame_summary: Frames rail's slipping share of transalpine freight as a policy problem in a growing market: road grows faster than rail, works in Germany constrain rail until about 2030, and wagonload traffic needs federal support.
verbatim_quote: Die Bahn hat im ersten Halbjahr 2026 mehr Güter durch die Alpen transportiert als im Vorjahr. Das Wachstum fiel mit 3,1 Prozent jedoch weniger hoch aus als im Strassentransport.
verbatim_list: Der Anteil der Bahn am alpenquerenden Güterverkehr ging leicht zurück und beträgt neu 68 Prozent.
Die Zahl der Lastwagenfahrten durch die Alpen stieg im gleichen Zeitraum um rund 7 Prozent auf 511'000.
Die Anzahl beladener Wagen ging im ersten Halbjahr 2026 gegenüber dem Vorjahressemester um 8 Prozent zurück.
SBB Cargo erzielte im ersten Halbjahr im EWLV einen Verlust von 12 Millionen Franken bei Abgeltungen von 40 Millionen Franken.
Der Schienengüterverkehr auf der Nord-Süd-Achse wird weiterhin durch die vielen Baustellen, vor allem in Deutschland, beeinträchtigt. Eine Entspannung zeichnet sich erst ab ca. 2030 ab.
notes: Swiss Federal Office of Transport media release with the H1 2026 transalpine semester report; German-language Tier 1 regional primary source for the multi-language pass.

title: Marktuntersuchung Eisenbahnen - Sonderausgabe Sommer 2026
key_claim: German rail freight performance fell 5.4% in 2025, driven by a collapse of more than 21% at DB Cargo whose restructuring shifted market share to the competitor railways, now 67% of the market.
frame_summary: Attributes the 2025 collapse in German rail freight performance to DB Cargo's restructuring, with competitor railways absorbing only part of the lost traffic and market share shifting durably to them.
verbatim_quote: Die Entwicklung im Schienengüterverkehr war maßgeblich von der DB Cargo beeinflusst. Der Rückgang der Verkehrsleistung fiel mit mehr als -21 Prozent noch deutlicher aus als der schon gravierende Rückgang der Betriebsleistung. Die Wettbewerberbahnen konnten einen Teil der Tonnenkilometer aufnehmen, sodass diese insgesamt gegenüber 2024 um 5,4 Prozent sanken.
verbatim_list: Im Schienengüterverkehr zeigten sich die Auswirkungen der Umstrukturierung bei DB Cargo, deren Betriebsleistung um rund 20 Prozent einbrach. Die Wettbewerberbahnen konnten einen Teil davon aufnehmen, sodass die Trassenkilometer im Schienengüterverkehr insgesamt gegenüber 2024 um rund 5 Prozent sanken.

Im Schienengüterverkehr verursachte der Einbruch bei DB Cargo eine weitere deutliche Marktanteilsverschiebung zugunsten der Wettbewerberbahnen auf nunmehr 67 Prozent, die damit nun zwei Drittel des SGV-Marktes darstellen.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band): the canonical regulator quantification of the German 2025 collapse that the 2026 evidence builds on. German-language Tier 1 regulator source.

title: CEO Bernhard Osburg: DB Cargo cannot meet EU break-even deadline
key_claim: DB Cargo's CEO says operational break-even in 2026, required under the EU state aid procedure, is out of reach after a roughly €260 million write-down on the UK sale, and restructuring should extend across its European operations, including 16 international subsidiaries.
frame_summary: Argues DB Cargo will miss the end-2026 EU break-even requirement because of the UK sale write-down, and that the company's response is to extend restructuring from Germany across all of its European operations.
verbatim_quote: DB Cargo is in a race against time to break-even. This is a requirement in an EU State Aid procedure against the company. By the end of this year, the freight operator needs to reach its financial goals, but that looks impossible now.
verbatim_list: The book value of the UK branch was around €260 million higher than what DB Cargo is expecting to recover from its sale. This will lead to an equal loss in the company’s 2026 financial performance.
Without the DB Cargo UK write-down, the company would have reached the break-even point this year, he said.
This includes 16 international subsidiaries.
notes: Reports Osburg's comments to dpa; the forcing event for the restructuring stage of the pathway.

title: Europe's rail freight problems are immediate, the Commission's solutions are not
key_claim: The Commission's measures for rail freight, state aid cover raised from 50% to 90% and a new timetabling system only from the end of 2030, with DAC not fully deployed until the early 2030s, do not provide relief in the near term while volumes fall in most EU countries.
frame_summary: Argues the Commission's remedies for rail freight are real but arrive years after the sector's immediate decline, leaving a near-term gap the announced measures do not cover.
verbatim_quote: Building new lines and terminals, deploying DAC and ERTMS, and what is left of the Greening Freight Package are all important measures, but do not provide immediate relief. They all require years of commitment and billions of euros, while the sector needs concrete action in the short term as well, as numbers are dropping in most EU countries.
verbatim_list: The new guidelines allow for a higher coverage, from 50% to 90% of the cost of a project, while the Regulation will introduce a new timetabling system, but only from the end of 2030.
Whatever opinion one might have of DAC, the main point is that it will not be fully deployed until the early 2030s at least.
notes: Policy-gap piece around the Commission's answer to MEP Krutílek; carries the timing of the capacity regulation's new timetabling system and the state aid guidelines used in the Counter-Argument.

title: UIRR Newsletter Q3.2026: CT still experiencing harsh turbulences
key_claim: European combined transport volumes fell again in Q3 2026, German corridors run at minimum capacity, German track access charges are set to rise around 12% in 2027 with 2028 rises of +85% for very heavy trains and +6.6% for regular trains, and the sector's 12-month business sentiment is negative.
frame_summary: Presents combined transport's renewed decline as the product of German infrastructure constraints, subpar alternative routes and rising track access charges on top of a weak economy, with member sentiment negative for the next twelve months.
verbatim_quote: The problems encountered are well known: infrastructure challenges, with German transport corridors only running at minimum capacity; extremely low water levels on the Rhine, leading to disruptions that also hit terminals; subpar alternative routes; and increasing track access charges. All of this coming on top of a negative economic environment, with low growth and high inflation.
verbatim_list: Over the past three months, the economic environment for Combined Transport has deteriorated further, recording volumes falling by 1,23% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
are still set to rise by around 12% in 2027
the track access charges in 2028 set to increase by +85% for very heavy trains and +6.6% for regular trains
However, based on the sentiment reported by UIRR members, the Business Sentiment Index of the European Combined Transport Community is negative for the next twelve months.
notes: Quarterly statistics newsletter of the combined transport operators' association; primary CT volume data, classified Tier 3 as an industry body. The 1,23% figure uses the newsletter's decimal comma.

title: Trassenpreise für Güterbahnen steigen 2027 um 12,9 Prozent
key_claim: DB InfraGO plans to raise 2027 track access charges by 12,9% for rail freight against a 7,9% average, after the Cologne administrative court allowed the rises to be passed on; the provisional 2028 target revenue implies a further double-digit average rise.
frame_summary: Reports DB InfraGO's planned 2027 track access rises, highest for freight, as a settled outcome of the regulatory and court process rather than an open question.
verbatim_quote: Besonders deutlich fällt die geplante Erhöhung im Schienengüterverkehr aus. Dort sollen die Trassenpreise, die als Nutzungsentgelt für das Schienennetz erhoben werden, um 12,9 Prozent steigen.
verbatim_list: Die Nutzung des deutschen Schienennetzes wird 2027 erneut teurer. Die DB InfraGo plant eine durchschnittliche Erhöhung der Trassenpreise um 7,9 Prozent.
Das Verwaltungsgericht Köln hatte erst in der vergangenen Woche entschieden, dass die Bahn die vorgesehenen Erhöhungen der Trassenpreise an die Verkehrsunternehmen weitergeben darf.

Auch für das Jahr 2028 rechnet die DB InfraGo zunächst mit höheren Erlösen aus den Trassenpreisen. Geplant ist derzeit ein Zielerlös von 8,6 Milliarden Euro. Rechnerisch würde dies einer durchschnittlichen Erhöhung der Entgelte um 15,1 Prozent entsprechen.
notes: dpa-sourced trade press report; German-language corroboration of the 2027 charge rise and the Verwaltungsgericht Köln ruling of late September 2026.

title: Ti, Upply & IRU European Road Freight Rate Benchmark report (Q2 2026 edition)
key_claim: European road freight contract rates reached 148.0 index points (+7.9 quarter on quarter) and spot rates 146.8 (+14.6) in Q2 2026, with operating costs up almost 10% year on year while road volumes stabilise.
frame_summary: Frames European road freight as repricing upward together on costs, with contract and spot rates rising in step while demand stabilises rather than recovers.
verbatim_list: 146.8 index points (+14.6 QoQ)
up almost 10% YoY (CNR index)
Road trade volumes fell just 1.6% YoY – a marked improvement on Q1’s 8% decline, suggesting demand is stabilising even as costs climb.
notes: Standing benchmark landing page for the quarterly Ti/Upply/IRU report; the page itself carries no publication date, so it is recorded as an evergreen reference accessed 06/11/2026. Quality data provider, Tier 2.
